reviews.review: I have been happy with the game so-far (only 2 hours at this time). It is a little clunky with the VR controls at times, but there is a lot of potential here. The fact that you can play with friends that don't have VR is amazing. The game is also challenging with a lot of funny moments. I tapped my hatchet in one hand with the gas can in my other... did not end well. I recommend this game because there are not many games like it and I would like to support the Devs in hopes that this might be a real success.

I played through the testing so i have more than a half an hour in the game.  
First of all, dont come in expecting perfection.  There is allot of jank to this game.  But i feel that the coop function and driving are really good.  

Pros
-COOP
-works well in VR.
-big world
-good foundation of a game
-a ton of effort in explaining the game
-constant updates.  Been in the testing phase for almost a year and the game has changed dramatically for the better.  

Cons
-works "okay" with desktop mode
-you may not like it playing solo
-lacks a story
-weapons sound does not "pack a punch"
-need more of a variety of enemies
-enemies feel..off...its hard to explain. I feel like i am shooing a paper bag, instead of a living being. 
-enemies need to look better

If you are a lurker, like I am, then this is the review for you. 

This game is made by a duo, two people. What has been achieved here is rather impressive with the amount of systems they have in place. From having a reliable Desktop and vr mode, to the humble animation of eating something, there are many things going on under the hood that many may miss. Sure, there are going to be bugs especially since this has just recently released on early access. 

Early access is meant to be a time to support the development, and to directly help shape the game. This game is no exception, the developers are wonderful human beings, who listen to you and genuinely enjoy spending time with people. One of the most impressive things I've seen these devs do, is on a few occasions, invite those who have negative experiences to the discord to chat about where the problems lie. These devs acknowledge there are problems and acknowledge that feedback is one of the more important tools in their toolbox. I see these devs going a long way with the attitudes I have observed thus far, even before I directly engaged with them. 

The game its self is extremely fun to play, there are small problems and annoyances, however none of them game breaking. There is in game local area voice chat. The game has quite a few game play loops, get lost? need to find your teammates? Use a flare gun, preferably at night and hope someone saw it. Need loot? Hungry? We better stop by these houses. Out of fuel? Guess we are hoofing it. Out of ammo? Run or break out the knife/axe, don't have either? You got fists don't you? 

The experiences I have already experienced in the 7 hours I have played, have been nothing but an enjoyment in VR and Desktop modes. I would highly suggest the game is played with friends, and if you have no one to play with, come by the discord. You'll find a link in the news section. 

Support these devs, they deserve it with how much passion they have for the games they make.

EDIT: Grammatical Corrections.

Edited/Update: I had a lot of fun running with the developers (Christian and Jes) the day after writing this review :D We completed my first (and currently only) escape. I've been playing it daily ever since, determined to stay alive as long as possible before completing a second escape. I've made it a few days. I just wanted to say this is a really unique game and if I may add a suggestion, I would really love to pick up the enemy heads after shooting them off. I've seen numerous basketball courts around the map and it would be a healthy pastime. It'd be better if I could put them in a backpack but I won't push it. I won't push it. You're the best.

On Quest 2: I've played this a little and started with the demo. It's a work in progress but leaning way more towards being a complete game. The maps are huge and I can't seem to get past the first night alone. After hosting and searching for sessions, I've found that it's best to host and hope for the best as of right now. It's a nice surprise when new players jump in and for the most part, they're excited to learn all of the Virtual Reality controls or a Non-VR run through.

The last map I played was really fun. I found the in-game physical map (which is the first objective and puts into perspective how big this map is) and an ammo station (second objective) where I found an LMG, heals, etc. It was late at night and after stashing everything, an alien beamed down not far from me. Within seconds I was rushed by a bunch of zombies I could barely make out. It was a terrifying virtual experience where I died quickly and wanted nothing more but to play another match.

Issues: When the backpack is filled with guns, ammo, hatchets and such, they tend to get in the way of my view while I'm walking around (While sitting). I've found a few ways around it like leaning back a little but, not really sure what to do about that. Also, It's a struggle with driving and flying vehicles. Most vehicles I can't figure out how to get them to work. It doesn't matter if I put gas in, use the wrench, etc. Maybe I just haven't played with it enough but I see the PC play-through and getting into vehicles and taking off looks like cake in them.

Some things I liked: The force-pull items to backpacks feature made a big difference. I like not having to bend over every time I see an apple. I also haven't had any issues with the controls whatsoever. Free motion movement and the smooth turning camera are essential in my opinion and the options menu lets you adjust everything. The guns feel fairly realistic and enemies attack rapidly, forcing you to quickly react and at times, end up throwing swings, and it works :) Food is plentiful and stamina is low. It's a challenging and well put together game really. Keep up the good work. I would recommend this to anyone and my hope is that more people will play this.
reviews.developer_response:
Hi MangoSun,

Thank you for the thorough and positive review, it means a lot to us!

Love reading the details of your story and how each time you played it unfolded differently.

Also happy to hear you enjoy the force pull inventory feature and that is working well for you.

To address three of your comments specifically:

1. Driving: Driving in VR involves pressing the red start button and gripping the lever and pushing it forward.

More details on this are in our online tutorial in the Movement and Interaction section starting at 9:25:

https://youtu.be/Nl6SN3wI4eY

2. Sitting in VR: We know there's a good amount of players that prefer to play sitting down, even I do especially for long periods of time. We'll look into making sitting something more ideal for people who need or want that option. Added this to our public Trello:

https://trello.com/c/dZasfyMb/23-user-suggested-features

3. Finding People to Play With: As it is still very early, it might be hard to find random games to jump into. We do have a Discord where you might be able to find a crew to play with. There's definitely people looking for groups to play with there.

https://discord.gg/BUjyZcd8

Again, really glad you found it an enjoyable challenge, and looking forward to hearing more for you in the future. Thank you.

Best,
Christian
